# prepspaces — Complete Technical Curriculum Manifest

> Website: https://prepspaces.com/
> Official Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/prepspaces/ (@prepspaces)
> Description: Comprehensive open educational curriculum covering 6 core systems engineering disciplines across 121 technical modules, architectural blueprints, interactive labs, and diagnostic frameworks.

---

# Track 1: System Design Masterclass

**Track Hub:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design
**Scope:** Comprehensive curriculum on large-scale distributed systems, high availability, database replication, microservices, consensus, traffic control, and architectural trade-offs.
**Total Modules:** 24

## Module 1: System Design Course & Architecture Interview Preparation
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design
- **Topic Summary:** Complete guide to designing scalable distributed systems, high availability, microservices, and system design interview questions.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 2: Requirements & Capacity Estimation Guide
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/requirements
- **Topic Summary:** Learn how to estimate throughput (QPS/RPS), storage volumes, bandwidth, and memory caches during system design interviews.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 3: Networking, APIs & Communication Protocols
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/networking
- **Topic Summary:** Deep dive into REST, gRPC, WebSockets, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, and TCP/UDP communication patterns in modern architectures.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 4: Monoliths vs Microservices Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/architecture
- **Topic Summary:** Compare monolithic architectures, modular monoliths, and microservices decomposition with real-world trade-off criteria.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 5: Relational Databases, NoSQL & Indexing Internals
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/databases
- **Topic Summary:** Master B-Trees, LSM-Trees, SQL indexing, NoSQL document/key-value stores, and database query optimization.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 6: Distributed Caching, Redis & CDN Strategies
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/caching
- **Topic Summary:** Master cache-aside, write-through, write-behind, LRU/LFU eviction, and distributed caching invalidation strategies.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 7: Database Replication, Partitioning & Sharding
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/replication
- **Topic Summary:** Master horizontal sharding, consistent hashing, single-leader vs multi-leader replication, and failover topologies.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 8: Object Storage, File Systems, Search Engines & Data Pipelines
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/storage
- **Topic Summary:** Master cloud object storage, distributed file systems, inverted index search engines, batch and streaming data pipelines, and modern lakehouse architecture.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 9: Distributed Systems, Clocks & Network Partitions
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/distributed-systems
- **Topic Summary:** Understand physical vs logical clocks (Lamport, Vector), network latency, timeouts, and CAP theorem nuances.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 10: Consistency Models, Linearizability & Quorum Systems
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/consistency
- **Topic Summary:** Deep dive into strict consistency, sequential consistency, causal consistency, eventual consistency, and quorum math (R+W > N).
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 11: Distributed Consensus & Raft Protocol
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/consensus
- **Topic Summary:** Interactive breakdown of distributed consensus, Paxos vs Raft, leader election, log replication, and split-brain defenses.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 12: Message Queues, Kafka & Event-Driven Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/messaging
- **Topic Summary:** Understand message brokers, RabbitMQ vs Apache Kafka, consumer groups, partitions, event sourcing, and delivery semantics.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 13: Distributed Transactions, 2PC & Saga Orchestration
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/transactions
- **Topic Summary:** Learn how to manage transactions across distributed microservices using Two-Phase Commit (2PC) and Saga patterns.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 14: Load Balancing, Rate Limiting & Traffic Management
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/traffic
- **Topic Summary:** Master L4/L7 load balancing algorithms, Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket rate limiting, circuit breakers, and backpressure.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 15: Scalability & Performance Modeling
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/scalability
- **Topic Summary:** Analyze system bottlenecks, vertical vs horizontal scaling, Amdahl's law, Universal Scalability Law, and performance tuning.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 16: Multi-Region Deployments & Disaster Recovery
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/multi-region
- **Topic Summary:** Design active-passive and active-active multi-region architectures, calculating RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 17: Reliability Engineering & Observability
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/reliability
- **Topic Summary:** Master metrics, distributed tracing, structured logging, SLA/SLO/SLI calculation, and high-availability design.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 18: System Design Security & Multi-Tenancy
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/security
- **Topic Summary:** Architect zero-trust networks, OAuth2/OIDC token verification, RBAC/ABAC authorization, and data isolation at scale.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 19: Real-Time Systems, WebSockets & Presence Servers
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/realtime
- **Topic Summary:** Design live presence platforms, collaborative editing architectures, and scalable WebSocket connection managers.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 20: Search Engines, Inverted Index & Vector Feeds
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/search
- **Topic Summary:** Understand inverted index engines (Elasticsearch), full-text retrieval, relevance ranking, and activity feed generation.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 21: AI Systems Design & Inference Serving at Scale
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/ai-systems
- **Topic Summary:** Architect production machine learning systems, model serving pipelines, GPU scheduling, vector databases, and RAG architectures.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 22: System Design Case Studies (URL Shortener, Chat, Feed)
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/case-studies
- **Topic Summary:** Full end-to-end architectural case studies: TinyURL shortener, real-time WhatsApp-style chat, and Twitter feed algorithms.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 23: Advanced System Design Case Studies (Uber, Netflix, Stripe)
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/advanced-case-studies
- **Topic Summary:** High-scale engineering deep dives: Ride-hailing dispatch, global video streaming CDN, and financial payment platforms.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 24: System Design Architecture Capstone Project
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/system-design/capstone
- **Topic Summary:** Synthesize all distributed system principles into a complete, enterprise-grade architecture specification and design doc.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

# Track 2: Cloud Computing Architecture

**Track Hub:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud
**Scope:** Enterprise public cloud architecture across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, covering VPC networking, serverless compute, storage, databases, and multi-cloud systems.
**Total Modules:** 13

## Module 1: Cloud Computing Course & Interview Preparation

## Module 2: Cloud Networking: VPCs, Subnets & Gateways

## Module 3: Cloud Compute: Virtual Machines to Serverless

- **Topic Summary:** Compare EC2 instances, spot instances, autoscaling groups, containers (ECS), and serverless execution models.

## Module 4: Cloud Storage: Object, Block & File Systems

- **Topic Summary:** Deep dive into AWS S3, EBS, EFS, storage lifecycle policies, encryption at rest, and cloud data tiering.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 5: Managed Cloud Databases: RDS, DynamoDB & Aurora
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/databases
- **Topic Summary:** Architect managed cloud database clusters with read replicas, multi-AZ failover, and global distributed tables.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 6: Well-Architected Cloud Framework
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/architecture

## Module 7: Deep AWS Engineering & Architecture Mastery
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/aws

## Module 8: Microsoft Azure Architecture & Enterprise Cloud
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/azure

## Module 9: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/gcp

## Module 10: Multi-Cloud Strategy & Hybrid Architectures

## Module 11: Cloud Security, IAM & Zero-Trust Governance
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/cloud/security
- **Topic Summary:** Enforce least privilege IAM, secret rotation, key management (KMS), and automated cloud security posture management (CSPM).

## Module 12: Cloud Economics & FinOps Cost Optimization

# Track 4: Operating Systems Master Course

**Track Hub:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os
**Scope:** University-informed systems engineering based on MIT, Stanford, and CMU curricula. Kernel architecture, CPU scheduling, virtual memory, concurrency, file systems, and Linux internals.
**Total Modules:** 24

## Module 1: Operating Systems Master Course
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os
- **Topic Summary:** Master operating systems internals, kernel architectures, process scheduling, virtual memory, concurrency, and Linux systems programming.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 2: Module 2: Computer Architecture for OS Engineers
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/architecture
- **Topic Summary:** Master CPU execution, registers, privilege rings, interrupts, MMU page translation, TLBs, DMA, and system boot stages.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 3: Module 3: C Programming & Systems Programming Model
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/systems-programming
- **Topic Summary:** Master C memory models, virtual address space layouts, ELF binaries, static and dynamic linking, AddressSanitizer, and POSIX system interfaces.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 4: Module 4: OS Interfaces, System Calls & Program Execution
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/syscalls
- **Topic Summary:** Master system call transitions, file descriptors, fork, execvp, waitpid, process lifecycle, signals, pipes, and strace diagnostics.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 5: Module 5: Processes and Process Lifecycle
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/processes
- **Topic Summary:** Master process abstractions, kernel task_struct (PCB), 5-state transitions, context switching, orphans, zombies, and Linux /proc exploration.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 6: Module 6: CPU Scheduling and Performance
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/scheduling
- **Topic Summary:** Master FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Round Robin, Multilevel Feedback Queues (MLFQ), context-switch overhead, CPU affinity, and Linux EEVDF.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 7: Module 7: Threads and Multithreaded Programming
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/threads
- **Topic Summary:** Master POSIX threads (pthreads), shared vs private state, threading models (1:1, N:1, M:N), Amdahl's Law, and cache false sharing mitigation.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 8: Module 8: Concurrency, Synchronization and Deadlocks
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/concurrency
- **Topic Summary:** Master race conditions, critical sections, POSIX mutexes, condition variables, semaphores, C11 memory ordering, Coffman deadlock conditions, and linearizability.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 9: Module 9: Memory Hierarchy and Memory Allocation
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/memory
- **Topic Summary:** Master virtual address spaces, stack frames, heap allocators, first-fit vs best-fit vs buddy allocation, fragmentation, and cache locality.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 10: Module 10: Virtual Memory and Address Translation
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/virtual-memory
- **Topic Summary:** Master hardware MMU address translation, hierarchical page tables, PTE flags, TLB hit rates, Effective Access Time (EAT), and Copy-on-Write.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 11: Module 11: Demand Paging and Page Replacement
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/demand-paging
- **Topic Summary:** Master demand paging, minor and major faults, working sets, thrashing, FIFO, Optimal, LRU, Clock, Belady's Anomaly, and Linux memory pressure.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 12: Module 12: Advanced Memory, Virtual Machines and Containers
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/virtualization
- **Topic Summary:** Master memory-mapped I/O, huge pages, NUMA nodes, hypervisors, EPT/NPT two-stage translation, Linux namespaces, and cgroup v2 memory limits.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 13: Module 13: Filesystems and Storage Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/filesystems
- **Topic Summary:** Master files, directories, inodes, dentries, extents, journaling, crash consistency, VFS, page cache writeback, fsync, and ext4/XFS/Btrfs design.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 14: Module 14: Storage Architecture, I/O Scheduling & Performance
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/storage
- **Topic Summary:** Master HDDs, flash SSDs, NVMe parallel queues, Little's Law, Linux I/O schedulers, DMA, write amplification, and io_uring.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 15: Module 15: IPC, Pipes, Shared Memory & Signals
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/ipc
- **Topic Summary:** Master interprocess communication, anonymous pipes, named FIFOs, Unix domain sockets, POSIX shared memory, semaphores, signals, and backpressure.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 16: Module 16: Crash Consistency, Durability and Recovery
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/crash-consistency
- **Topic Summary:** Master crash consistency, page cache write ordering, fsync, atomic file replacement, journaling, copy-on-write, and disaster recovery validation.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 17: Module 17: Kernel Architecture & System Implementation
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/kernel-architecture
- **Topic Summary:** Master kernel internals, boot flow from UEFI to PID 1, system-call dispatch tables, trap handling, spinlock interrupt safety, and MIT xv6 vs Linux.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 18: Module 18: Linux Internals & Performance Diagnostics
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/diagnostics
- **Topic Summary:** Master Linux performance diagnostics, /proc, /sys, vmstat, iostat, perf, strace, PSI stalls, and evidence-based bottleneck triage.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 19: Module 19: OS Networking & Network I/O
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/networking
- **Topic Summary:** Master the Linux kernel network stack, TCP/UDP sockets, non-blocking I/O, epoll event loops, socket buffers, application backpressure, and network namespaces.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 20: Module 20: OS Security, Isolation & Reliability
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/security
- **Topic Summary:** Master Linux identities, capabilities, POSIX permissions, cgroup v2 limits, seccomp filters, Secure Boot, DoS defenses, and STRIDE threat modeling.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 21: Module 21: Advanced Synchronization & Multiprocessor Systems
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/advanced-sync
- **Topic Summary:** Master multiprocessor synchronization, spinlocks, atomics, lock-free queues, memory ordering, cache coherence, false sharing, NUMA, and RCU.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 22: Module 22: OS Design, Testing & Failure Analysis
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/testing
- **Topic Summary:** Master systems testing, component invariants, fault injection, ThreadSanitizer race detection, kernel panics, and performance regression gates.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 23: Module 23 Capstone: Build an OS Component (xv6/RISC-V)
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/capstone
- **Topic Summary:** Build, extend, and test an educational operating system component using MIT xv6 on RISC-V, system call traps, and engineering verification.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 24: Module 24: Final Capstone
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/os/final-capstone
- **Topic Summary:** Culminating operating systems engineering project. Implement bounded concurrent worker queues, performance diagnostic tools, or virtual memory simulators.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

# Track 5: Computer Networks & Internet Architecture

**Track Hub:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks
**Scope:** University-level networking based on MIT, Stanford, UC Berkeley, CMU, and Princeton. Physical transmission, Ethernet, IPv4/IPv6, BGP routing, TCP/UDP sockets, DNS, and network security.
**Total Modules:** 24

## Module 1: Module 1: Introduction to Computer Networks & Internet Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks
- **Topic Summary:** Master computer networks from physical signals and Ethernet switching to global BGP routing, packet switching math, TCP/IP protocols, and network security.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 2: Module 2: Network Models
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks/models
- **Topic Summary:** Master OSI 7-layer and TCP/IP 4-layer network models, protocol encapsulation, router frame re-framing, Wireshark packet dissection, and layered troubleshooting.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 3: Module 3: Physical Layer & Data Transmission
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks/physical
- **Topic Summary:** Master physical layer signals, Nyquist and Shannon channel capacity, optical power budgets, line coding (NRZ, Manchester, PAM-4), and ethtool transceiver diagnostics.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 4: Module 4: Data Link Layer & Ethernet Switching
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks/datalink
- **Topic Summary:** Master Ethernet frame structures, CAM table MAC learning, ARP resolution, 802.1Q VLAN trunking, Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), and Layer 2 link security.
- **Target Competencies:** Systems architecture, engineering trade-offs, failure modes, implementation patterns, and verification.

## Module 5: Module 5: IPv4 Addressing, Subnetting & Enterprise Planning
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/networks/ipv4

# Track: Blockchain Technology & Decentralized Systems (24 Modules)
> University-style curriculum based on Stanford CS251, MIT, UC Berkeley, Cornell, and NIST IR 8202.
> Track Overview: https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain

## Module 1: Introduction to Blockchain Technology
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain
- **Alternative URL:** https://prepspaces.com/courses/blockchain
- **Level:** Beginner to Intermediate | Theory + Practical | 6–8 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Centralized vs decentralized systems, distributed ledger technology (DLT), cryptographic hashing, SHA-256 properties, block anatomy, block linking, tamper-evident chains, and building a Python blockchain from scratch.
- **Key Concepts:** SHA-256 collision resistance, pre-image resistance, avalanche effect, Previous Hash linking, cryptographic verification, state machine replication.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live interactive 4-block blockchain visualizer, real-time tampering simulator, and production-grade Python script with canonical JSON serialization and tamper detection.

---

## Module 2: Cryptography Fundamentals for Blockchain
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/cryptography
- **Alternative URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/crypto
- **Level:** Beginner to Intermediate | Mathematics + Programming | 10–12 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Mathematical foundations of cryptography, modular arithmetic, prime fields, finite groups, SHA-256 vs Keccak-256 vs SHA3-256, symmetric vs asymmetric encryption, secp256k1 elliptic curve scalar multiplication, ECDSA signing and verification, nonce reuse vulnerabilities, HD wallets (BIP-32), Ethereum and Bitcoin P2PKH address generation, binary Merkle trees, and logarithmic inclusion proofs.
- **Key Concepts:** One-way preimage and collision resistance, avalanche effect, ECDLP discrete log hardness, ECDSA (r, s) formulation, RFC 6979 deterministic nonces, X9.62 public key serialization, domain-separated Merkle proofs.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live interactive Merkle tree builder with visual sibling proof explorer, live private key and address derivation simulator, and complete Python toolkit with zero third-party blockchain dependencies.

---

## Module 3: Distributed Systems & Consensus Mechanisms
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/consensus
- **Alternative URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/distributed-systems
- **Level:** Intermediate | Theory + Mathematics + Programming | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Distributed computing fundamentals, node communication and failure models (crash, omission, timing, Byzantine), the Byzantine Generals Problem (n >= 3f + 1), Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) and quorum intersection (Q = 2f + 1), Proof of Work (PoW) mining difficulty and expected attempts, Nakamoto consensus and heaviest chain selection, Proof of Stake (PoS) validator committees, Gasper and slashing, Proof of Authority (PoA), Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) pre-prepare/prepare/commit phases, temporary forks, chain reorganizations (reorgs), probabilistic vs explicit finality, Sybil attacks and defense, network partitions, Brewer's CAP theorem (CP vs AP), and the Fischer-Lynch-Paterson (FLP) impossibility result.
- **Key Concepts:** Safety vs liveness, quorum intersection (Q = 2f + 1), cumulative work fork choice, 16^d difficulty scaling, 2/3 stake supermajority, PBFT view changes, orphan blocks, mempool recycling, 51% attack threshold, selfish mining, asynchronous agreement impossibility.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live interactive Byzantine Generals simulator with customizable traitors and quorum verification, real-time in-browser SHA-256 Proof of Work mining sandbox with tamper detector, Proof of Stake validator lottery and committee approval visualizer, CAP theorem network partition sandbox, and complete Python implementations of Proof of Work (`proof_of_work.py`) and Proof of Stake (`proof_of_stake.py`).

---

## Module 4: Bitcoin Architecture, Transactions & UTXO Model
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/bitcoin-utxo
- **Level:** Intermediate | Theory + Systems Engineering | 10–12 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Bitcoin architecture, Unspent Transaction Output (UTXO) accounting model, transaction scripts (Script), mempool, block verification, Coinbase transactions, and halving cycles.
- **Key Concepts:** UTXO graph, Script stack execution (OP_DUP, OP_HASH160, OP_EQUALVERIFY, OP_CHECKSIG), P2PKH, P2SH, SegWit (BIP-141), transaction fees, block serialization.
- **Hands-On Lab:** UTXO pool visualizer, Bitcoin Script stack execution simulator, and transaction verification engine.

---

## Module 5: Ethereum & EVM Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/ethereum-evm
- **Level:** Intermediate | Theory + Architecture | 10–12 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM), state transitions, account model, world state trie, Patricia Merkle trees, gas schedule, EIP-1559 fee market, and smart contracts.
- **Key Concepts:** Account state (nonce, balance, storageRoot, codeHash), modified Merkle Patricia Trie (MPT), gas limit vs gas price, base fee burning, priority tip, uncle blocks, and PoS consensus.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live EVM state transition simulator, Patricia Trie lookup inspector, and EIP-1559 gas fee calculator.

---

## Module 6: EVM Deep Dive & Opcode Execution
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/evm-internals
- **Level:** Advanced | Low-Level Systems | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** 256-bit EVM stack machine, volatile memory allocation, non-volatile storage slot layout, SSTORE/SLOAD gas mechanics, call opcodes (CALL, STATICCALL, DELEGATECALL), and bytecode disassembly.
- **Key Concepts:** Stack overflow/underflow, memory expansion quadratic cost, storage collision vectors, EVM word alignment, fallback and receive functions, revert reasons, and assembly Yul.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Interactive step-by-step EVM stack/memory/storage debugger and Yul bytecode tracer.

---

## Module 7: Solidity Programming Fundamentals
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/solidity
- **Level:** Intermediate | Programming | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Solidity 0.8+ syntax, value types, reference types (memory, storage, calldata), visibility specifiers, view and pure functions, function modifiers, events, custom errors, and contract inheritance.
- **Key Concepts:** ABI encoding/decoding, arithmetic checked math, reentrancy guards, event emission topics, interface definition, abstract contracts, and error handling with revert.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Browser-based Solidity compiler sandbox with unit assertion checking.

---

## Module 8: Advanced Solidity & Gas Optimization
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/advanced-solidity
- **Level:** Advanced | Optimization & Security | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Storage slot packing (256-bit word packing), calldata vs memory optimization, assembly Yul implementations, unchecked arithmetic blocks, memory caching of storage variables, ERC-7201 namespaced storage, and immutable patterns.
- **Key Concepts:** SLOAD/SSTORE gas reduction, tight variable packing, transient storage (EIP-1153), calldata slice manipulation, bitwise operations for permissions, and custom assembly routines.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live gas benchmark comparator demonstrating 40%+ gas reduction across baseline vs optimized contracts.

---

## Module 9: Smart Contract Development & Architecture
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/architecture
- **Level:** Advanced | Systems Design | 12–15 hours
- **Topic Summary:** End-to-end decentralized application architecture: factory pattern, registry pattern, pull payments over push payments, escrow state machines, OpenZeppelin integration, UUPS and Transparent upgradeable proxies, and The Graph event indexing.
- **Key Concepts:** Proxy delegatecall mechanisms, EIP-1967 storage slots, storage collision prevention, initialization vs constructor, emergency circuit breakers, and state machine transitions.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Interactive proxy upgrade simulator with storage slot validation.

---

## Module 10: Smart Contract Testing & Security
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/testing
- **Level:** Advanced | Quality Assurance | 10–12 hours

- **Key Concepts:** Invariant testing, fuzz test input generation, vm.prank and vm.deal cheatcodes, stateful vs stateless fuzzing, coverage analysis, and CI/CD testing pipelines.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live fuzz test runner diagnosing invariant violations.

## Module 11: Wallets, Keys & Transaction Signing
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/blockchain/wallets-keys
- **Level:** Intermediate | Cryptography & Security | 10–12 hours
- **Topic Summary:** Hierarchical Deterministic (HD) wallets (BIP-32), mnemonic seed phrases (BIP-39), standard derivation paths (BIP-44), ECDSA transaction signing, EIP-1559 envelopes, EIP-712 typed structured data signing, Sign-In with Ethereum (SIWE), and nonce management.
- **Key Concepts:** Entropy to mnemonic generation, master node derivation, public vs private child keys, replay attack mitigation (EIP-155), and typed structured hashes.
- **Hands-On Lab:** Live BIP-39 mnemonic generator, BIP-44 address explorer, and EIP-712 signing simulator.

  - 19. Production Airflow Deployment (Dev vs Prod, Docker containerization, Kubernetes Helm deployment, production checklist)

## Module 17: Stream Processing and Real-Time Analytics
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/data-engineering/stream-processing
- **Topics Covered:**
  - 1. Introduction to Stream Processing (Continuous processing over unbounded events, operations: filter, transform, enrich, aggregate, join, pattern detection, message consumption vs stream processing)
  - 2. Batch Processing vs Stream Processing (Scheduled batches vs continuous stream, latency budgets, Lambda architecture: batch/speed/serving layers, Kappa architecture: streaming-first replay)
  - 3. Bounded and Unbounded Datasets (Finite collected datasets vs infinite streams, continuous computation as evolving queries, stateful aggregation requirements)
  - 4. Real-Time Processing Architecture (Sources, Kafka ingestion, streaming engine, operational/analytical storage, serving layer, end-to-end pipeline latency budgets)
  - 5. Event Time vs Processing Time (Event time at source, processing time at worker, ingestion time at broker, mobile offline buffering scenario, time synchronization and NTP)
  - 6. Windowing Concepts (Logical grouping of unbounded streams, tumbling, sliding, session window abstractions)
  - 7. Tumbling Windows (Fixed-size, non-overlapping time intervals, Flink SQL TUMBLE syntax, use cases)
  - 8. Sliding Windows (Fixed duration with smaller slide intervals, overlapping events, state memory multipliers, Flink SQL HOP syntax)
  - 9. Session Windows (Activity bursts, dynamic durations, inactivity gap thresholds, Flink DataStream EventTimeSessionWindows, session merging)
  - 10. Watermarks (Temporal progress tracking: Watermark = max(EventTime) - AllowedDelay, window finalization, state cleanup, distributed watermark minimums)
  - 11. Out-of-Order Events (Network delays, parallel partitions, retries, revenue correction workflows)
  - 12. Late-Arriving Events (Watermark boundary crossing, allowed lateness window retention, side outputs, reconciliation)
  - 13. Stateful Stream Processing (Stateless vs stateful, customer transaction counters, keyed state, operator state, window state, RocksDB state backend, State TTL eviction)
  - 14. Stream Joins and Aggregations (Grouped and windowed aggregations, stream-stream joins with time bounds, stream-static joins, temporal joins, Flink SQL and PySpark syntax)
  - 15. Checkpointing and Recovery (Periodic state snapshots, recovery workflows, Flink checkpoint barriers aligned/unaligned, checkpoints vs savepoints, Spark checkpointLocation)
  - 16. Exactly-Once Processing Concepts (At-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once boundaries, Flink two-phase commit sinks, Spark foreachBatch batchId deduplication, idempotent PostgreSQL upserts)
  - 17. Apache Flink Architecture (JobManager: ResourceManager, Dispatcher, JobMaster; TaskManagers, Task Slots resource scheduling, operator chaining, parallelism, RocksDB state backend, deployment modes)
  - 18. Spark Structured Streaming (Incrementally updated tables, micro-batch execution, Continuous Processing, Real-time mode in Spark 4.1+, Kafka source integration, JSON parsing, Append/Update/Complete output modes)
  - 19. Apache Flink vs Spark Structured Streaming (Architectural comparison, continuous vs micro-batch, event-time capabilities, selection criteria)
  - 20. Streaming Data Pipelines (Streaming ETL vs traditional ETL, quality validation: schema, nulls, range, duplicate detection, freshness monitoring, backpressure)
  - 21. Real-Time Analytics Dashboards (Window aggregation for visualization efficiency, metrics: revenue, transactions, operational lag; frontend updates: polling, SSE, WebSockets)

## Module 16: Event-Driven Architecture and Apache Kafka

- **Topics Covered:**
  - 1. Introduction to Event-Driven Architecture (EDA principles, events vs commands, loose coupling, real-world e-commerce use cases, traditional vs event-driven)
  - 2. Event-Based Communication (Producer-consumer models, event anatomy, notification vs event-carried state transfer, choreography vs orchestration, microservices boundaries)
  - 3. Messaging Systems (Why messaging is needed, decoupling, buffer capabilities, Kafka vs RabbitMQ vs AWS SQS vs Google Cloud Pub/Sub)
  - 4. Message Brokers and Queues (Brokers, queues, point-to-point vs publish-subscribe, work queues vs Kafka durable commit logs, selection criteria)
  - 5. Introduction to Apache Kafka (History at LinkedIn, persistent append-only logs, high throughput, real-time data pipelines position)
  - 6. Kafka Brokers and Clusters (Broker responsibilities, cluster topology, bootstrap servers, brokers vs KRaft controllers, KRaft quorum vs ZooKeeper deprecation in Kafka 4.x)
  - 7. Topics and Partitions (Topic definitions, partitions as ordered append-only logs, parallelism math, offsets, sizing guidelines, partition expansion hazards)
  - 8. Producers and Consumers (Record anatomy: key, value, headers, partition, timestamp, Python producer confluent-kafka, delivery callbacks, Python consumer, manual commits)
  - 9. Consumer Groups (Parallel consumption, partition assignment rules: Max Active <= Partitions, multiple consumer groups, rebalance protocol, eager vs cooperative rebalance)
  - 10. Offset Management (Consumer position vs committed offset, auto-commit hazards, manual synchronous/asynchronous commits, auto.offset.reset earliest/latest/none, CLI offset inspection & resets)
  - 11. Message Ordering and Partition Keys (Per-partition FIFO guarantees, key-based Murmur2 hashing, banking sequential transactions, hot partition skew mitigation)
  - 12. Replication and Fault Tolerance in Kafka (Replication factor N, leader vs follower replicas, In-Sync Replicas ISR, min.insync.replicas, leader election failover)
  - 13. Kafka Retention Policies (Time-based retention.ms, size-based retention.bytes, delete cleanup vs Log Compaction, tombstone null-value deletion records)
  - 14. Producer Acknowledgements (acks=0, acks=1, acks=all, interaction with min.insync.replicas, latency vs durability trade-offs, production tuning)
  - 15. Delivery Semantics (At-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once processing, idempotent producer PID and sequence numbers, Kafka transactions vs external databases)
  - 16. Schema Registry (Why schema governance matters, architecture, subjects -key/-value, compatibility modes: BACKWARD, FORWARD, FULL, NONE, transitive compatibility)
  - 17. Avro and JSON Serialization (JSON trade-offs, Apache Avro binary serialization, nullable union schemas with defaults, Schema Registry wire format 5-byte framing)
  - 18. Kafka Connect (Source vs Sink connectors, workers, tasks, converters, Single Message Transforms SMT, standalone vs distributed mode, REST API configuration)
  - 19. Kafka Connect CDC — Change Data Capture (Query vs Trigger vs Transaction-log CDC, Debezium PostgreSQL/MySQL WAL capture, operation codes c/u/d/r, snapshot coordination)
  - 20. Dead-Letter Queues (Poison pill message isolation, retriable vs non-retriable exceptions, retry topic backoff delays, DLQ contextual metadata, alerting metrics)
  - 21. Message Replay (Reprocessing workflows, replay via new consumer group vs offset reset, time-based replay, idempotent consumer processing prerequisites)
  - 22. Kafka Security (Authentication: SASL/PLAIN/SCRAM/TLS/OAuth, encryption in transit TLS, authorization ACLs, principal permissions, audit logging)
  - 23. Real-Time Event Ingestion Architecture (Batch vs Real-time, end-to-end pipeline architecture, e-commerce payment flow, fraud detection, metrics: consumer lag, throughput)
  - 24. Practical Kafka Laboratory (Docker apache/kafka:4.4.0 KRaft setup, CLI topic management, Python producer/consumer scripts, consumer lag inspection, offset resets, compacted topics)
  - 25. Kafka Message Processing Internals (Append-only logs, log segment rolling, zero-copy kernel transfer via sendfile, sparse index files .index and .timeindex, producer batching batch.size and linger.ms, compression zstd/lz4/snappy)
  - 26. Kafka Transactions and Exactly-Once Processing (Transactional producers, transactional.id, 2-phase commit transaction coordinator, read_committed isolation level, atomicity across outputs and consumed offsets)
  - 27. Kafka Monitoring and Observability (Broker, producer, consumer metrics, consumer lag formula Lag = LogEndOffset - CommittedOffset, Prometheus, Grafana, JMX metrics)
  - 28. Designing a Production Event-Driven Data Platform (E-commerce architecture case study, 10M daily events, end-to-end component walkthrough)
  - 29. Important Kafka Design Decisions (13 core architectural decision matrix: topics, partitions, keys, replication, retention, serialization, CDC, DLQ, security)
  - 30. Important Architectural Patterns Around Kafka (Event Sourcing vs EDA, dual-write problem, Transactional Outbox pattern, Saga pattern orchestrator vs choreography)
  - 31. End-to-End Capstone Project (Real-Time E-commerce Data Streaming Platform: tech stack, topics, functional requirements, evaluation rubric)
  - 32. Common Mistakes in Kafka and Event-Driven Systems (20 critical production pitfalls: treating Kafka as queue, assuming global ordering, ignoring consumer lag, neglecting security)
  - 33. Important Interview Questions and Answers (40 comprehensive technical interview questions and scenario-based system design answers)
  - 34. Recommended Learning Resources (Official Kafka 4.4 documentation, Kafka Connect, Confluent Schema Registry, Debezium, GitHub repositories)
  - 35. Final Revision — Module 16 (30-topic revision matrix covering all core event streaming concepts)
  - 36. How Module 16 Connects to Your Data Engineering Roadmap (Progression to Advanced Stream Processing with Apache Flink and Spark Streaming)

## Module 15: Distributed Systems for Data Engineers
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/data-engineering/distributed-systems
- **Topics Covered:**
  - 1. Introduction to Distributed Systems (Single-machine limitations vs distributed cluster, workload division, partial failure, concurrency, scalability, 10-item overhead trade-offs)
  - 2. Distributed Computing Architecture (Client-server, multi-tier presentation/application/data layers, master-worker coordinator model, peer-to-peer, microservices boundaries, vertical vs horizontal scaling)
  - 3. Distributed Processes and Communication (IPC mechanisms, synchronous request-response vs asynchronous messaging, network failure modes, latency vs throughput, performance metrics)
  - 4. Client-Server Architecture and Remote Procedure Calls (RPC internal mechanics, client/server stubs, serialization, gRPC over HTTP/2, Protocol Buffers, JSON-RPC, XML-RPC, RPC vs REST, failure modes)
  - 5. Network Communication and Serialization (Serialization workflows, JSON, XML, Apache Avro schemas, Protobuf IDL, Apache Parquet columnar storage, TCP connection-oriented reliability vs UDP datagrams, serialization payload size math)
  - 6. Distributed Storage Systems (HDFS NameNode and DataNode block architecture, block sizing, S3 object storage buckets and keys, distributed databases Cassandra/Spanner/CockroachDB, storage vs computing separation)
  - 7. Data Partitioning (Partition pruning, horizontal vs vertical partitioning, range partitioning, hash partitioning (Hash(Key) % N), list partitioning, round-robin, sharding vs partitioning, data skew and hot partition mitigation)
  - 8. Data Replication (Replication factor N, synchronous replication acknowledgements vs asynchronous replication lag, failover risks, replication in Kafka/Cassandra/Postgres, replication vs point-in-time backups)
  - 9. Leader and Follower Architecture (Primary-replica write coordination, leader reads vs follower reads, failover mechanisms, split-brain problem and fencing, multi-leader regional replication conflicts)
  - 10. Consistency Models (Strong consistency, linearizability vs serializability, eventual consistency convergence, read-your-writes, monotonic reads, monotonic writes, consistency levels comparison)
  - 11. Strong Consistency and Eventual Consistency in Practice (E-commerce race conditions, inventory reservation vs product view counts, business operation consistency mapping)
  - 12. CAP Theorem (Consistency linearizability, Availability, Partition Tolerance trade-offs, CP vs AP behaviors during network split, PACELC theorem, common CAP misconceptions)
  - 13. Quorum-Based Systems (Read/write quorum formula R+W>N, strict overlap proof, majority voting Q=floor(N/2)+1, fault tolerance thresholds, Cassandra tunable consistency)
  - 14. Fault Tolerance (Hardware, software, network, data, and human failures, redundancy, checkpointing in distributed compute engines, fault tolerance vs high availability)
  - 15. Failure Detection (Heartbeats, adaptive timeouts, false positive detections, liveness, readiness, and dependency health checks, failure detection vs recovery)
  - 16. Consensus Fundamentals (Agreement, validity, termination, safety vs liveness, Raft consensus algorithm: leader election, candidate states, replicated log replication, Paxos comparison)
  - 17. Distributed Coordination (Distributed locks, lease expiration, fencing tokens for stale worker protection, coordination services ZooKeeper, etcd, Consul)
  - 18. Retry Mechanisms and Idempotency (Fixed-delay, exponential backoff formula Delay=Base*2^attempt, jitter randomness against thundering herds, mathematical idempotency f(f(x))=f(x), idempotency keys, SQL ON CONFLICT upserts, idempotency vs exactly-once)
  - 19. Backpressure (Producer-consumer throughput imbalance, queue accumulation, flow control, rate limiting, buffering, Kafka consumer lag metrics, Spark Streaming micro-batch rate limits, backpressure vs buffering)
  - 20. Message Delivery Guarantees (At-most-once, at-least-once with retry duplication, exactly-once transactional scope, Kafka idempotent producer, transactional commits, consumer offset management commit strategies)
  - 21. Distributed System Reliability (Reliability vs availability, uptime formula, the 5 nines 99.999% downtime tables, single points of failure, load balancing, bulkheads fault isolation, circuit breaker states CLOSED/OPEN/HALF-OPEN, disaster recovery RPO and RTO, SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs)
  - 22. Putting Everything Together: Real-World Distributed Data Engineering Architecture (Complete real-time e-commerce architecture mapping all 21 distributed systems principles across Kafka, Python workers, distributed storage, and analytics)
  - 23. Practical Laboratory (Lab 1: Python Multiprocessing Worker Pool, Lab 2: Dockerized Apache Kafka Messaging, Lab 3: Leader-Follower Replication Simulation, Lab 4: Enterprise Event Processing Platform Mini-Project)
  - 24. Common Mistakes in Distributed Systems (15 Production fallacies: assuming distributed is faster, ignoring idempotency, treating retries as harmless, CAP misinterpretations, omitting fencing tokens, etc.)
  - 25. Important Interview Questions and Answers (30 Comprehensive technical interview Q&As with full system design explanations)
  - 26. Recommended Learning Resources (Official documentation for Kafka, Spark, Hadoop, gRPC, Cassandra, Raft, PostgreSQL, etcd, Kubernetes)
  - 27. Final Revision — Module 15 (Complete 21-topic revision summary table)
  - 28. How Module 15 Connects to Other Data Engineering Modules (Direct bridge to Kafka streaming, Spark distributed computing, and Lakehouse architectures)

  - 18. Pipeline Dependency Management (Task dependencies, Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAG), Apache Airflow PythonOperator, Dagster, Prefect, Step Functions)
  - 19. Large-Scale Batch Processing Architecture (Distributed cluster, Driver, Executors, Cluster Managers, Partitions, Narrow vs Wide transformations, Shuffle cost, Data Skew, AQE)
  - 20. Building End-to-End ETL Pipelines (Multi-source extraction, raw landing, data validation, transformation, Gold publication, monitoring)

Practical Major Project: Enterprise E-commerce ETL and Batch Processing System (PostgreSQL schema, sample data, Python parquet extraction, Bronze storage, PySpark Silver cleaning, multi-table enrichment, Gold analytics, incremental watermarking, idempotency, Airflow DAG orchestration, reconciliation)

### Module 9: Data Ingestion and Change Data Capture (CDC)
- **Canonical URL:** https://prepspaces.com/learning/data-engineering/ingestion-cdc
- **Topics Covered:**
  - 1. Introduction to Data Ingestion (Source diversity, reliability, performance, fault tolerance, e-commerce flow)
  - 2. Data Ingestion Architectures (6 tiers: Sources, Extraction, Transport, Processing, Destination, Orchestration; push vs pull)
  - 3. Batch Data Ingestion (Scheduled intervals, bulk processing, Python/Pandas extraction, tradeoffs)
  - 4. Incremental Data Ingestion (Watermarking, timestamps, increasing IDs, modified timestamps, boundary overlap handling)
  - 5. Full Load vs Incremental Load (Initial snapshotting, ongoing change sync, comparison matrix)
  - 6. Database Ingestion Strategies (Full table, range-based, parallel, partition extraction, connection pooling)
  - 7. API-Based Ingestion (REST HTTP methods, Bearer/OAuth authentication, cursor vs offset pagination, rate limits, exponential backoff)
  - 8. File-Based Ingestion (Directory scanning, manifest files, object-finalization notifications, validation, quarantine)
  - 9. Cloud Storage Ingestion (S3, ADLS, GCS, EventBridge/SQS object event notifications, cross-cloud transfers)
  - 10. Change Data Capture (CDC) Foundations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE events, timestamp polling vs triggers vs log-based CDC)
  - 11. Log-Based CDC Architecture (Database transaction logs, MySQL row-based Binlog, PostgreSQL WAL logical decoding & replication slots)
  - 12. Source-to-Target Data Movement (Mapping definitions, type conversions, record count validation, financial reconciliation)
  - 13. Data Extraction Strategies Decision Matrix
  - 14. Watermarks and Offsets (Persistent watermark tables, compound cursors, Kafka partition offsets, consumer groups)
  - 15. Checkpointing (Saving stream progress and state, Spark Structured Streaming checkpoint directory, Kafka offset commits)
  - 16. Duplicate Event Handling (Root causes: network retries, crash replays; primary key deduplication, window functions)
  - 17. Idempotent Ingestion (MERGE / upsert statements, event sequence numbers, exactly-once vs idempotency)
  - 18. Schema Changes During Ingestion (Confluent Schema Registry, backward/forward/full compatibility, semantic drift)
  - 19. Error Handling and Dead-Letter Queues (Retryable vs permanent errors, DLQ payload structures, exponential backoff with jitter)
  - 20. Designing Scalable Ingestion Systems (Horizontal scaling, Kafka partitioning, backpressure management, micro-batching, monitoring)
  - 21. Practical Project: Build a Real-Time CDC Ingestion Pipeline (MySQL -> Binlog -> Debezium -> Kafka -> Delta Lakehouse)
  - 22. Common Ingestion Mistakes & Production Anti-Patterns
